name: PERCENTILE
description: PERCENTILE returns the k-th percentile of values in a dataset using the inclusive method. It is the legacy function, retained for compatibility.
tldr: Returns the value at a given percentile (k from 0 to 1, inclusive).

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array of numeric values.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: The percentile value, a number between 0 and 1 inclusive (e.g. 0.5 for the median).

basicExample.explanation: Using the inclusive method the rank is 1 + 0.5*(4-1) = 2.5, interpolated between 2 and 3 to give 2.5.

advancedExamples.title: 25th percentile with exact position
advancedExamples.description: When the computed rank lands on an integer, the value at that position is returned.
advancedExamples.explanation: Rank = 1 + 0.25*(5-1) = 2, so the 2nd value, 2, is returned.

advancedExamples.title: 75th percentile with interpolation
advancedExamples.description: A non-integer rank is linearly interpolated.
advancedExamples.explanation: Rank = 1 + 0.75*(4-1) = 3.25; interpolate 25% from the 3rd to the 4th value: 3 + 0.25*(4-3) = 3.25.

howItWorks: PERCENTILE uses the inclusive (INC) method. It calculates a rank position as 1 + k*(n-1), where n is the count of values, then interpolates linearly between the surrounding sorted values. k must be between 0 and 1 inclusive; k=0 returns the minimum and k=1 returns the maximum. This function is equivalent to PERCENTILE.INC. Text and logical values in the array are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the percentile.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =PERCENTILE(range, k) with k between 0 and 1.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The interpolated percentile value is returned.

limitations: k must be between 0 and 1 inclusive; values outside this range cause #NUM!.
May linearly interpolate between data points, returning a value not present in the data.
Ignores text and logical values in the array.

commonErrors.cause: k is less than 0 or greater than 1, or the array is empty.
commonErrors.fix: Use a k value between 0 and 1 and ensure the range contains numbers.

commonErrors.cause: Interpolation between two data points is by design.
commonErrors.fix: This is expected; the percentile need not be an actual data value.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports PERCENTILE with the same inclusive behavior as legacy Excel.

faq.question: Is PERCENTILE the same as PERCENTILE.INC?
faq.answer: Yes. PERCENTILE is the legacy name and PERCENTILE.INC was added in Excel 2010; both use the inclusive method.

faq.question: Why might the result not be in my data?
faq.answer: The inclusive method interpolates between the two nearest values when the rank is fractional.

faq.question: What does k = 0 or k = 1 return?
faq.answer: k = 0 returns the minimum value and k = 1 returns the maximum value.
